identity.what_it_is: NYC Parks' public Atlantic beach and Riegelmann Boardwalk in Coney Island, Brooklyn; Parks lists it together with Brighton Beach as 'Coney Island and Brighton Beach'.
identity.where: Brooklyn, on the Atlantic Ocean, from W. 37th Street to Ocean Parkway (Parks beach page).
identity.warnings: Parks manages Coney Island and Brighton Beach as one listing; Manhattan Beach is a separate Parks beach with its own rules. The Manhattan Beach rules in the bundle are NOT Coney rules. Pages on nyc.gov were captured at the end of the 2026 season, so 'open now' wording is stale (beaches closed until Memorial Day weekend 2027).

spike_candidates.statement: On July 6, 2026 Coney Island's water tested at 227 enterococci per 100 mL, over double the 104 limit, and reporters found one small boardwalk sign.
spike_candidates.tension: The city says swimming is not recommended, yet people on the sand were still entering the water with little on-site warning; the beach stays open, only swimming is advised against.

spike_candidates.statement: Two teenage sisters vanished in the water off Coney Island shortly after 8 p.m. on July 5, 2024, two hours after lifeguards left at 6 p.m.
spike_candidates.tension: The beach and boardwalk run 24 hours with Parks staff on site, but swimming is only guarded from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., and red-flag warnings were already posted.

spike_candidates.statement: Coney Island is the only NYC beach with a 24-hour Parks operation, but the water is lifeguarded only 8 hours a day.
spike_candidates.tension: A Parks commissioner calls it the safest feeling place at night, while every recent local drowning story hinges on the hours when lifeguards are off.

spike_candidates.statement: The F/Q West 8th Street-NY Aquarium stop is the southernmost station in the whole NYC subway, and its 700-foot aquarium bridge was torn down in 2013.
spike_candidates.tension: The closest-to-the-sea stop carries only about a fifth of Stillwell Avenue's riders (679,646 vs 3,475,833 in 2024) and lost its direct pedestrian link to the aquarium.

facts.fact: Parks defines the Coney Island and Brighton Beach beach as running along the Atlantic from W. 37th Street to Ocean Parkway; the Parks beach office number is (718) 946-1350.
facts.quote: on atlantic ocean, from w. 37th street to ocean parkway
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Parks describes the beach as nearly three miles of sand with courts for beach volleyball, handball and basketball.
facts.quote: nearly three miles of sandy beaches, or check out the courts for beach volleyball, handball, and basketball
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Lifeguards are on duty daily from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. during beach season.
facts.quote: during beach season, lifeguards are on duty daily, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Swimming is prohibited when lifeguards are off duty and in closed sections, which are marked with signs and/or red flags.
facts.quote: swimming is prohibited when lifeguards are not on duty and in closed sections.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Parks' online beach status map for the summer is refreshed each morning shortly after 10 a.m. based on lifeguard availability and conditions; red flags and signs on the sand mark closed areas.
facts.quote: this map is updated each morning, soon after 10:00 a.m., based upon lifeguard availability and current beach conditions
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: The boardwalk is closed 1:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. per the Parks amenities list.
facts.quote: boardwalk: yes (closed 1:00 a.m.-5:00 a.m.)
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Parks lists a concession stand as an amenity at the beach.
facts.quote: concession stand: yes
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: For 2026 Parks says beaches are open from Memorial Day weekend through September 13, 2026.
facts.quote: beaches are open from memorial day weekend through september 13, 2026.

facts.fact: The standing season rule is Memorial Day weekend through the Sunday after Labor Day.
facts.quote: beaches are open from memorial day weekend through the sunday after labor day.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: All NYC public beaches are free and open to the public.
facts.quote: all of our beaches are free and open to the public.

facts.fact: NYC Parks maintains 14 miles of beaches in total, across eight beaches.
facts.quote: parks maintains 14 miles of beaches.

facts.fact: Parks runs a free SPF 30 sunscreen program at all eight city beaches.
facts.quote: nyc parks is excited to continue its free sunscreen program located at all eight beaches.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Parks lists only metered street parking for the beach.
facts.quote: parking metered street parking
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Parks calls the beach accessible, with beach mats for wheelchair access and beach wheelchairs by reservation only.
facts.quote: this is an accessible beach. beach mats are available for wheelchair access.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Coney Island has beach mats at W 33rd, W 32nd, W 29th and W 22nd Streets, Stillwell Avenue, W 5th and W 8th Streets and Ocean Parkway.
facts.quote: coney island beach mat: west 33rd street, west 32nd street, west 29th street, west 22nd street, stillwell avenue, west 5th street, west 8th street and ocean parkway, brooklyn

facts.fact: Brighton Beach has beach mats at Brighton 2nd and 6th Streets, Coney Island Avenue and Brighton 15th Street.
facts.quote: brighton beach beach mat: brighton 2nd street, brighton 6th street, coney island avenue and beach 15th street, brooklyn

facts.fact: Beach wheelchairs have three oversized wheels, adjustable seats, and push and pull handles for the move from boardwalk to sand; they must be pushed.
facts.quote: beach wheelchairs use three oversized wheels to roll over the sand

facts.fact: Beach wheelchairs can be used only from Memorial Day through the Sunday after Labor Day, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily.
facts.quote: wheelchairs can only be used from memorial day through sunday after labor day, from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Beach wheelchair request form

facts.fact: Beach wheelchair use is free for up to three hours by reservation.
facts.quote: wheelchairs are available for up to three (3) hours of use free of charge.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Beach wheelchair request form

facts.fact: Reservations are online or by phone at (718) 885-2275; the same number appears on Parks' beaches list for Orchard Beach in the Bronx, so it may be a citywide line or a copy-paste.
facts.quote: reservations can be made online or by calling (718) 885-2275.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Beach wheelchair request form

facts.fact: Parks asks for 48 hours' notice for a beach wheelchair but may fill last-minute requests on site depending on availability; reservations are strongly advised on summer weekends and holidays.
facts.quote: although last-minute onsite requests on the day of your visit may be accommodated, depending on availability
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Beach wheelchair request form

facts.fact: Users must leave ID with Parks staff on site when picking up a beach wheelchair.
facts.quote: identification is required and must be left with the nyc parks staff on-site.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Beach wheelchair request form

facts.fact: Beach wheelchair rules: an attendant aged 18 or older must be present and the chair may go only to the water's edge, never into the water.
facts.quote: wheelchair users must have an attendant 18 years or older present when occupied and in use.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Beach wheelchair request form

facts.fact: Beach wheelchairs must not be taken into the water.
facts.quote: wheelchairs must not be taken into the water - only up to the water's edge.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Beach wheelchair request form

facts.fact: One Coney Island wheelchair pickup point is at W 8th Street and the Riegelmann Boardwalk, opposite the NY Aquarium; others are at W 5th, Stillwell, W 22nd, W 29th, W 32nd, W 33rd and Ocean Parkway.
facts.quote: coney island beach - west 8th street and riegelmann boardwalk (opposite ny aquarium)
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Beach wheelchair request form

facts.fact: Off-season, Parks says to check back two days before Memorial Day weekend to reserve a beach wheelchair.
facts.quote: check back to reserve a beach wheelchair two (2) days before next memorial day weekend.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Beach wheelchair request form

facts.fact: Brooklyn's beaches opened for the 2026 season on Saturday, May 23 at 10 a.m., ahead of Memorial Day weekend.
facts.quote: brooklyn's beaches will officially reopen for the season on saturday, may 23 at 10 a.m., just in time for memorial day weekend.
facts.source_title: Brownstoner/Brooklyn Paper - Brooklyn beaches officially open this weekend

facts.fact: Brownstoner reports lifeguards in chairs 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. every day until September 13, 2026, described as a week after Labor Day.
facts.quote: lifeguards will be in their chairs from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. every day until september 13, a week after labor day.

facts.fact: Luna Park and Deno's Wonder Wheel opened in March 2026 and the Cyclones' first pitch was in early April, so the beach is the last piece of Coney Island to open each year.
facts.quote: its iconic amusement parks, luna park and deno's wonder wheel, opened back in march

facts.fact: Brownstoner says the beach is the last part of Coney Island to open for the season.
facts.quote: the beach is the last part of coney island to open for the season.

facts.fact: Lifeguard shortages in recent years sometimes closed sections of beach temporarily and in some cases for weeks.
facts.quote: in recent years, ongoing lifeguard shortages have sometimes forced the city to close sections of beach temporarily - or, in some cases, for weeks at a time.

facts.fact: In 2025 NYC had more than 1,000 lifeguards on its beaches and pools, the most since 2019.
facts.quote: there were more than 1,000 lifeguards staffing new york city beaches and pools last year, the highest number since 2019

facts.fact: Lifeguard recruits rose 23 percent in 2025 after a new union contract and more recruiting.
facts.quote: recruits were up 23 percent from the year before.

facts.fact: City pools open June 27, 2026, more than a month after beaches; Parks keeps certifying lifeguards until July.
facts.quote: new york city public pools don't open until june 27, more than a month after the beaches.

facts.fact: Parks Commissioner Tricia Shimamura said Coney Island is the only NYC beach with a 24-hour Parks operation.
facts.quote: coney island is the only place where we have a 24 hour operation.

facts.fact: Shimamura said her first real NYC memories were on this beach and recalled a late-night visit where it was full of people.
facts.quote: my first real core new york city memories were here on this beach,

facts.fact: On a late weeknight the beach was crowded with people walking, playing, holding snakes and doing magic tricks.
facts.quote: instead, she said, it was packed with people walking, playing, holding snakes, and doing magic tricks.

facts.fact: Shimamura said the safety she felt came from seeing Parks enforcement, police, FDNY and EMTs there at all hours.
facts.quote: that means no matter what time you come to this beach, you will see parkies out doing the jobs that they need to do.

facts.fact: Brooklyn Borough Parks Commissioner Marty Maher joked the Atlantic is the biggest air conditioner in the world.
facts.quote: biggest air conditioner in the world

facts.fact: Council Member Kayla Santosuosso called Coney Island the people's beach on this side of town, a dig at Riis Beach.
facts.quote: the people's beach... on this side of town,

facts.fact: Brighton Beach is described as the quieter, less touristy beach a short walk down the sand from Coney.
facts.quote: a short walk down the sand is the quieter, less touristy brighton beach.

facts.fact: Manhattan Beach, at the end of the peninsula, is small and family-focused with picnic tables and grills.
facts.quote: the small, family-focused manhattan beach, which offers picnic tables and grills

facts.fact: Parks debuted purpose-made UTVs in 2026 so lifeguards can drive themselves and gear across the sand to emergencies.
facts.quote: shimamura also debuted new utvs

facts.fact: At the 2026 opening, officials turned on the water at the spray shower.
facts.quote: city officials turned on the water at the spray shower.

facts.fact: Opening week had abnormally scorching temperatures, about 90 F on the day of the Coney visit, while Memorial Day weekend was forecast cool and rainy.
facts.quote: after days of abnormally scorching temperatures this week, memorial day weekend is slated to be cool and rainy in new york city

facts.fact: As of the capture, the DOH page says NYC public beaches are closed for the season and reopen Memorial Day weekend 2027.
facts.quote: public beaches will reopen memorial day weekend 2027.

facts.fact: The Health Department samples water weekly at beaches, but Rockaway and Breezy Point only biweekly.
facts.quote: we take water samples at all beaches weekly except for at rockaway and breezy point beaches, where we take samples biweekly.

facts.fact: Sampling begins one month before the beach season starts.
facts.quote: beginning one month before beach season, the department collects weekly water samples

facts.fact: A yellow-sign advisory means swimming and wading are not recommended; a red-sign closure means they are not allowed.
facts.quote: advisory - swimming and wading not recommended (yellow sign)

facts.fact: Red-sign closures mean swimming and wading are not allowed.
facts.quote: closed - swimming and wading not allowed (red sign)

facts.fact: An advisory can be triggered by rain exceeding a beach's set threshold, which is how heavy rain ends up closing the water to swimmers even when samples have not come back.
facts.quote: rainfall exceeds the rainfall thresholds.

facts.fact: During an advisory the beach itself stays open; only swimming and wading are not recommended.
facts.quote: this means swimming and wading are not recommended, but the beach is open.

facts.fact: On July 9, 2026 New York City warned people to stay out of the water at a dozen beaches after a week of heavy rain.
facts.quote: new york city is warning people to stay out of the water at a dozen beaches because of elevated bacteria levels after all of the rain this week.
facts.source_title: ABC7 - A dozen NYC beaches warn of high bacteria levels

facts.fact: ABC7 found no beach announcements about the advisory and only one small sign on the boardwalk; a visitor said they should warn people more.
facts.quote: the advisory even applies to wading, but there have been no announcements on the beach.
facts.source_title: ABC7 - A dozen NYC beaches warn of high bacteria levels

facts.fact: ABC7 reported Coney's bacteria at about 227 versus an average near 20 per 100 mL, more than ten times higher.
facts.quote: the bacteria sat at around 227, more than 10 times higher
facts.source_title: ABC7 - A dozen NYC beaches warn of high bacteria levels

facts.fact: The New York State sanitary code caps enterococci at 104 colonies per 100 mL for a single sample.
facts.quote: the new york state sanitary code sets a maximum allowable threshold for acceptable amounts of enterococci at 104 colonies per 100 milliliters for a single water sample.
facts.source_title: Fox Weather - Over a dozen NYC beaches under swimming advisory

facts.fact: Coney Island's July 6, 2026 sample read 227, more than double the 104 standard.
facts.quote: when sampled on july 6, the water at coney island came in at 227-which is more than double the maximum health standard.
facts.source_title: Fox Weather - Over a dozen NYC beaches under swimming advisory

facts.fact: Of 18 locations under advisory in July 2026, Coney Island, South Beach and Midland Beach were named; the Staten Island beaches read in the thousands.
facts.quote: both midland beach and south beach measured enterococci counts in the thousands.
facts.source_title: Fox Weather - Over a dozen NYC beaches under swimming advisory

facts.fact: Enterococci are an indicator of fecal pollution and usually do not cause illness themselves but warn of more dangerous germs.
facts.quote: while enterococci bacteria themselves usually do not cause illness, their presence acts as a warning sign
facts.source_title: Fox Weather - Over a dozen NYC beaches under swimming advisory

facts.fact: A Northwell infectious-disease chief said the most common problem from swallowing contaminated water is a stomach illness.
facts.quote: the most common problem is swallowing the water and getting a gastrointestinal illness, virus or bacterial infection.
facts.source_title: ABC7 - A dozen NYC beaches warn of high bacteria levels

facts.fact: Two teenage sisters, 17 and 18, drowned off Coney Island on Friday July 5, 2024 after entering the water amid rip-current warnings once lifeguards were off duty.
facts.quote: two teenage sisters drowned in the waters off coney island on friday, police said - both had entered the water amid rip current warnings and after lifeguards went off duty.
facts.source_title: Gothamist - 2 teenage sisters drown off Coney Island

facts.fact: The sisters disappeared from view shortly after 8 p.m., two hours after the 6 p.m. lifeguard end time; divers recovered them.
facts.quote: police said the sisters entered the water and disappeared from view shortly after 8 p.m. on friday.
facts.source_title: Gothamist - 2 teenage sisters drown off Coney Island

facts.fact: Gothamist counted about 13 drownings off Rockaway in five years, all but one when lifeguards were off duty; the top advice was not to swim without lifeguards.
facts.quote: about 13 people have drowned off of rockaway's beaches in the last 5 years. all but one died when lifeguards were off duty, according to a gothamist analysis.
facts.source_title: Gothamist - 2 teenage sisters drown off Coney Island

facts.fact: Gothamist said the most important warning from experts was not to go in the water if no lifeguards are on duty.
facts.quote: but the most important warning was not to go in the water if no lifeguards are on duty.
facts.source_title: Gothamist - 2 teenage sisters drown off Coney Island

facts.fact: On July 12, 2024 News 12 reported red-flag warnings at Coney Island with swimming off limits and saw swimmers in the ocean with no lifeguards on duty.
facts.quote: news 12 observed no lifeguards on duty during the warning and swimmers in the ocean.
facts.source_title: News 12 Brooklyn - Officials warn Brooklyn swimmers of life-threatening rip current conditions

facts.fact: The July 2024 rip-current warnings ran until 6 p.m. Saturday and the currents can carry away even the most skilled swimmer.
facts.quote: the currents are strong enough to carry away even the most skilled swimmer.

facts.fact: On July 27, 2023 lifeguards saw two boys in distress in a no-swimming area near W 22nd Street just before 12:45 p.m.
facts.quote: on thursday, on-duty lifeguards observed two boys in distress in the water in a no swimming area of the beach near west 22nd street just before 12:45 p.m.
facts.source_title: ABC7 - Teen swimmer still missing at Coney Island

facts.fact: Parks said that section was under a red flag at the time and a preliminary police report pointed to rip currents.
facts.quote: officials with the parks department said that section of coney island was under a red flag at the time.
facts.source_title: ABC7 - Teen swimmer still missing at Coney Island

facts.fact: A 14-year-old was pulled out alive and his 15-year-old brother was lost; the NYPD harbor unit searched the next day and the body was found by July 30.
facts.quote: rescuers pulled a 14-year-old from the water who is expected to be ok.
facts.source_title: ABC7 - Teen swimmer still missing at Coney Island

facts.fact: CBS reported the editor's note that the missing 15-year-old's body was found on the Coney Island beach.
facts.quote: editor's note 7/30: body of missing 15-year-old swimmer found at coney island beach
facts.source_title: CBS New York - No sign of boy who got caught in rip current

facts.fact: In July 2023 Parks Commissioner Sue Donoghue said NYC had only 800 lifeguards for eight beaches and 48 pools, so some beach areas were closed.
facts.quote: nyc parks commissioner sue donoghue said the city only has 800 lifeguards for eight beaches and 48 public pools across the five boroughs.

facts.fact: Donoghue said Coney Island has lifeguards at six bays, with other areas unavailable for swimming because of the shortage.
facts.quote: we have lifeguards at six bays across coney island and we have 800 lifeguards across the city.

facts.fact: Despite red flags and danger signs, families still waded in the day after the 2023 loss; one said they were only putting their feet in because it was hot.
facts.quote: we're just putting our feet in, we're not going too far. it's hot,

facts.fact: A Coney Island resident said many nearby buildings have no air conditioning, so people go to the water to cool off.
facts.quote: many of these buildings don't have air conditioners. you're hot, you're gonna try to find ways to cool off,

facts.fact: Swim Strong Foundation advice: a rip current looks like a calm spot between busy water on either side.
facts.quote: a rip current will look like a calm spot between a lot of action happening on either side of it,

facts.fact: Rip currents pull you out, not under, and if caught you should stay calm and float on your back.
facts.quote: while they don't pull you down, they do pull you out, and pull you out very quickly,

facts.fact: Closed beach sections are marked with red flags meaning do not swim, and swimmers are told to obey lifeguards and leave the water in bad weather.
facts.quote: closed sections of the beach are indicated by red flags which mean do not swim.
facts.source_title: ABC7 - Teen swimmer still missing at Coney Island

facts.fact: At Manhattan Beach, swimming is allowed only when a lifeguard is on duty and red flags mean no swimming; Coney's rules PDF was not harvested.
facts.quote: swimming and bathing are allowed only when a lifeguard is on duty. red flags indicate no swimming or bathing.

facts.fact: Manhattan Beach (not Coney) bans dogs except service animals on beach and promenade from Memorial Day weekend to Oct 1.
facts.quote: dogs, except service animals, on beach and promenade from memorial day weekend to oct. 1

facts.fact: Manhattan Beach also bans alcohol, smoking, and open flame outside designated areas; these are not confirmed for Coney.
facts.quote: barbecuing and open flame except in designated areas

facts.fact: Manhattan Beach also prohibits fins, rafts and flotation devices except bodyboards, and jet skis, kayaking and paddleboarding.
facts.quote: snorkels, fins, rafts, unauthorized watercraft, and other flotation devices (except bodyboards)

facts.fact: The Parks park page puts the beach and boardwalk property from Corbin Pl. to W. 37 St., with 399.47 acres and ZIP codes 11224 and 11235.
facts.quote: corbin pl. to w. 37 st., boardwalk
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk

facts.fact: Off-season sights Parks names are the historic Riegelmann Boardwalk and the iconic Parachute Jump.
facts.quote: take a walk along the historic riegelmann boardwalk, gaze up at the iconic parachute jump
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk

facts.fact: Facilities at the park include public restrooms and spray showers (exact locations not given).
facts.quote: public restrooms spray showers wi-fi hot spots
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk

facts.fact: A 332-foot-long, ten-foot-tall cast-concrete sculpture wall was installed outside the aquarium in 1992.
facts.quote: 332-foot long, ten-foot tall cast-concrete sculpture wall installed outside the aquarium in 1992
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk

facts.fact: Parks scores the site 87 for park condition and lists $37.6M in recent investment.
facts.quote: 87 park condition score $37.6m recent investment
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk

facts.fact: A stale Parks news item on the page still says the 8 public beaches open Saturday May 28 (a 2022 date).
facts.quote: new york city's 8 public beaches open for the summer starting saturday, may 28
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk

facts.fact: The Brooklyn Cyclones play at the ballpark by the beach; Parks' beach page still calls it MCU Park (formerly KeySpan Park).
facts.quote: the mcu park (formerly keyspan park) baseball stadium where you can see the brooklyn cyclones play ball
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Coney Island-Stillwell Avenue is served by D, F, N and Q trains, with Brighton, Culver, Sea Beach and West End line tracks.
facts.quote: bmt brighton line ind culver line bmt sea beach line bmt west end line

facts.fact: Stillwell is an elevated station at 1243 Surf Avenue with four island platforms and eight tracks.
facts.quote: platforms 4 island platforms tracks 8

facts.fact: Stillwell's lines opened in stages from September 5, 1917 (Sea Beach) to May 1, 1920 (Culver), and the terminal was rebuilt and reopened May 29, 2005.
facts.quote: rebuilt may 29, 2005

facts.fact: Stillwell had 3,475,833 subway riders in 2024.
Buses serving Stillwell are B36, B64, B68, B74, B82, X28 and X38; the station is listed as accessible.
facts.quote: nyct bus: b36, b64, b68, b74, b82, x28, x38

facts.fact: West Eighth Street-NY Aquarium is the southernmost station in the whole NYC subway system.
facts.quote: this station is geographically the southernmost station in the entire new york city subway system.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: F and Q trains stop at W 8th St at all times, with an extra F during peak rush hours.
facts.quote: it is served by the f and q trains at all times, and by the < f > train during rush hours in the peak direction.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: W 8th St had 679,646 riders in 2024, about a fifth of Stillwell's volume.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The W 8th St station opened May 19, 1919; Brighton trains began serving it June 13, 1919.
facts.quote: opened may 19, 1919
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: In 1954 the transit authority announced a 700-foot overpass to the planned aquarium, with an estimated cost of $500,000 and completion by November 1955.
facts.quote: the estimated cost for the project was $500,000, and it was expected to be completed by november 1955.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The station closed August 2002 and reopened May 23, 2004 during the Stillwell rebuild.
facts.quote: the station was closed in august 2002 in conjunction with the reconstruction of the coney island-stillwell avenue terminal, and service was restored on may 23, 2004.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The pedestrian bridge to the aquarium was torn down August 8, 2013 for safety reasons and replaced by a crosswalk and wider sidewalks.
facts.quote: the pedestrian bridge was torn down on august 8, 2013, due to safety issues.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The W 8th St station has a 2005 artwork called Wavewall by Vito Acconci.
facts.quote: the 2005 artwork here is called wavewall by vito acconci.
facts.source_title: Wikipedia - West Eighth Street-New York Aquarium station

facts.fact: The Aquarium (602 Surf Ave) says take F or Q to W 8th St, or N/D to Stillwell then walk two blocks east on Surf.
facts.quote: take the f or q train to the west 8th street station on coney island, brooklyn. alternatively, take the n or d trains to the coney island-stillwell avenue station, then walk two blocks east on surf ave.

facts.fact: The B36 stops at Surf Ave and W 8th St, and the B68 at Neptune Ave and W 8th St.
facts.quote: take the b36 to surf ave. and west 8th st. or take the b68 to neptune ave. and west 8th st.

facts.fact: In summer, Surf Avenue traffic is regulated so cars can only turn left into the aquarium lot, approaching westbound from Ocean Parkway.
facts.quote: during the busy summer season, traffic on surf avenue is regulated to only allow for a left turn into the aquarium parking lot.

facts.fact: Driving from Manhattan: Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel, BQE west, exit 22 to Belt Pkwy east, exit 7 (Ocean Pkwy) to Surf Ave.
facts.quote: take exit 22 to the belt pkwy east.

facts.fact: From Long Island and Queens take the Belt Parkway west to exit 7B and Ocean Parkway to Surf Avenue.
facts.quote: take the belt pkwy west to exit 7b (ocean pkwy).

facts.fact: From Staten Island, the Verrazzano route uses exit 7S to Ocean Parkway south.
facts.quote: to belt pkwy east to exit 7s (ocean pkwy south).

facts.fact: Deno's Wonder Wheel sits on the boardwalk between the original Nathan's and the New York Aquarium.
facts.quote: between the original nathan's famous hot dog restaurant and the new york aquarium.

facts.fact: Deno's directions from Stillwell: head toward the beach, climb to the boardwalk, turn left and walk one block.
facts.quote: when you get up to the boardwalk, turn left and walk one block.

facts.fact: Deno's site gives the 2026 park opening as April 12 with kiddie rides at 11 a.m. and adult rides at noon.
facts.quote: park opens april 12. kiddie park opens at 11am and adult rides open at noon.

facts.fact: The street was renamed Denos Vourderis Place (formerly W. 12th St.), Deno's phone is 718 372 2592.
facts.quote: denos vourderis place (formerly w. 12th st.)

facts.fact: Rip-current guidance from the National Weather Service is linked from Parks' beach page.
facts.quote: rip currents - safety tips and information provided by the national weather service regarding the dangers of rip currents.
facts.source_title: NYC Parks - Coney Island and Brighton Beach

facts.fact: Sick after swimming? The Health Department says seek care and report it to 311.
facts.quote: if you suspect you got sick after swimming at a beach, seek medical attention promptly and report your illness by calling 311.

facts.fact: Even when swimming is banned, walking, running and sitting on the sand and boardwalk are allowed during regular park hours.
facts.quote: even when swimming and wading is not permitted, exercise such as walking and running, and spending time on the sand and boardwalk, are permitted during regular park hours.

facts.fact: Parks lets you sign up for Notify NYC beach notifications for real-time openings and closings.
facts.quote: to receive real-time opening and closing notifications

facts.fact: An advisory notice reads that swimming and wading are not recommended and directs people to 311 or nyc.gov/notifynyc.
facts.quote: one or more new york city area beaches are currently under an advisory.
facts.source_title: NYC Emergency Management - Notify NYC beach advisory

facts.fact: The DOH data portal says each beach is sampled every week and Rockaway/Breezy Point twice each week.
facts.quote: each beach is monitored and sampled every week, except for rockaway and breezy point beaches, which are sampled twice each week.
facts.source_title: NYC EH Data Portal - Beach water quality

facts.fact: Each bathing beach needs a Health Department permit and is inspected for compliance during the swim season.
facts.quote: a permit is required from the nyc health department for each bathing beach and its facilities.

recency.newest_item: Parks and Health Department pages captured around Sept 13 - Oct 2026 show the 2026 season is over; beaches reopen Memorial Day weekend 2027. Newest dated events are the July 6-9, 2026 bacteria advisory and the May 23, 2026 opening.

conflicts: Beach extent: Parks beach page says W. 37th Street to Ocean Parkway (V001) while the park page says Corbin Pl. to W. 37 St. (V082); Brighton is listed within the same beach listing. Parks 'nearly three miles' (V002). The beach page is more authoritative for swimming limits; the park page for property.

Water sampling frequency: DOH beach page says Rockaway/Breezy Point biweekly (V047) while the DOH data portal says twice each week (V117). All sources agree other beaches, including Coney, are sampled weekly; prefer the current DOH beach page, treat 'biweekly' as ambiguous.

Ballpark name: Parks beach page uses MCU Park (formerly KeySpan Park) (V088) while the park page and Brownstoner use Maimonides Park (the Brownstoner quote is in the bundle but not a fact id). Prefer 2026 press and the park page; the beach page's naming is stale.

Opening dates for amusement parks: Brownstoner says Luna Park and Deno's opened in March 2026 (V029) while Deno's own site says park opens April 12 (V110). Prefer Deno's own site for Deno's hours; unresolved for March.

Bacteria comparisons differ by baseline: ABC7 says 227 is more than 10 times the usual ~20 (V055), Fox says 227 is more than double the 104 limit (V057). Both are consistent; do not say 10x the limit.
Wheelchair phone (718) 885-2275 (V020) is also Orchard Beach's number on Parks' beaches list; unresolved whether it is citywide.

Season end: Parks says through September 13, 2026 (V008); generic rule is the Sunday after Labor Day (V009); Brownstoner calls it a week after Labor Day (V028). Labor Day 2026 was Sept 7, so all three agree on Sept 13.
W 8th St dates: station opened May 19, 1919 (V097) but Brighton trains began serving June 13, 1919 (same source); not a real conflict, specify which.
Lifeguard numbers: about 800 in 2023 (V071) vs more than 1,000 in 2025 (V032); different years, not a conflict.

2023 incident detail: CBS says witnesses saw the boys knee-deep, ABC7 says they were playing near rocks and were swept under in a no-swimming area (V067, V073); both from press, reconcile as reported by witnesses.
DOH page text carries both 'nyc beaches are open' and 'closed for the season' (V046); the second is current for Oct 2026.
